statements.status_notes: uv 0.13.7 uses rsa 0.9.10 only through reqsign-core 3.3.2, reqsign-google 3.2.0 and reqsign-azure-storage 3.3.0 for RSA signatures. Their production paths call SigningKey.sign_with_rng with OsRng; rsa 0.9.10 forwards that RNG to its private-key operation and enables RSA blinding against timing attacks. These callers do not use RSA decryption or its padding-rejection paths, so the Marvin decryption oracle is not reachable. See https://docs.rs/crate/reqsign-core/3.3.2/source/src/jwt.rs, https://docs.rs/crate/reqsign-google/3.2.0/source/src/sign_request.rs, https://docs.rs/crate/rsa/0.9.10/source/src/pkcs1v15/signing_key.rs, https://docs.rs/crate/rsa/0.9.10/source/src/pkcs1v15.rs and https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/626.

The rsa dependency in uv 0.13.7 is used by reqsign-core 3.3.2, reqsign-google 3.2.0 and reqsign-azure-storage 3.3.0 for RSA signatures. Those callers use SigningKey with sign_with_rng and an operating-system RNG; they do not perform RSA decryption. The Marvin padding oracle concerns PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption and implicit rejection, which these authentication paths do not exercise. See https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/626 and the decryption-only scope described at https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/pull/702.

The rsa crate is used transitively by reqsign for cloud credential signing. RustSec reports a timing side channel in private-key operations and no patched release. The applicability of these operations in uv remains under investigation; signing is not assumed immune. https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html

The Marvin timing side-channel leaks private-key material through non-constant-time private-key operations, so reaching it requires the process to hold and use an RSA private key. The rsa crate is present only as a transitive dependency of jsonwebtoken, which apollo-mcp-server uses solely to verify inbound JWTs against public keys fetched from a JWKS endpoint (jsonwebtoken::decode in crates/apollo-mcp-server/src/auth/valid_token.rs). The tree contains no RSA private-key API at all: no from_rsa_pem, no from_rsa_der and no RsaPrivateKey construction anywhere, and the only jsonwebtoken::encode calls sit inside #[cfg(test)] modules that are not compiled into the release binary and use HMAC secrets rather than RSA keys. No configuration exposes a signing or decryption path, so the vulnerable private-key code has no caller in the shipped artifact.

RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin timing side channel on RSA private-key operations) has no fixed release of the rsa crate: 0.9.10 is the newest stable and the rewrite lands only in the 0.10 pre-releases, a breaking line change inside the sspi and picky dependency tree. Teleport's desktop access RDP client reaches rsa 0.9.10 through its smart card emulation (lib/srv/desktop/rdp/rdpclient/src/piv.rs) and through sspi for CredSSP. Whether the timing of those private-key operations is observable by a party other than the Windows host being logged into is under review; the crate is tracked for an upstream fix.

CVE-2023-49092 (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, the Marvin attack) is a timing side channel in the rsa crate's private key operations with no patched release as of rsa 0.9.10. Milvus 3.0 includes rsa through reqsign in the milvus-storage bridge, which uses it only to sign Google Cloud Storage and Oracle OCI requests with the operator's own service account key; the exposure is limited to those deployments and remains under evaluation while upstream tracks a constant-time implementation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html

uv pulls in the rsa crate through Google service-account signing support. The advisory is for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption; uv uses RSA signing for registry authentication workflows, matching existing uv VEX prior art.
